title: Experiences of Porting Structured and Unstructured Stencil Applications to FPGA using SYCL
problem: Porting stencil applications to FPGAs using single-source languages (SYCL) may sacrifice productivity or performance; unclear if FPGAs are viable for low-arithmetic-intensity stencils.
motivation: SYCL promises portable GPU/CPU/FPGA code; but FPGAs have different memory hierarchies and resource constraints; need empirical evaluation on realistic stencil kernels.
method: SYCL stencil implementation: structured and unstructured grids, optimized for CPU (AMD) and FPGA (Intel Stratix 10), benchmarked on both, analyzing resource usage and performance.
key_novelty: Empirical evaluation of SYCL portability to FPGAs; identification of low-arithmetic-intensity kernel limitations on FPGAs.
contributions: SYCL stencil implementations for CPU and FPGA
Evidence of FPGA performance gaps for low-intensity kernels
primary_theme: FPGA viability for low-intensity stencil kernels via SYCL
